title: A Map of Shade
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: In an imaginary city, students notice that two routes of equal length can feel very different on a hot afternoon.
sentences.ja: 架空の都市で生徒は同じ長さの二つの道でも暑い午後には体感が異なると気づく。

sentences.en: One route follows a broad street with little protection from the sun, while the other passes beneath mature trees.
sentences.ja: 一方は日差しを遮るものが少ない広い通りで、もう一方は成長した木々の下を通る。

sentences.en: They decide to examine how a map might communicate this difference to people choosing where to walk.
sentences.ja: 地図が歩く道を選ぶ人にこの違いをどう伝えられるか調べることにする。

sentences.en: Their project begins with a discussion of what ordinary maps leave out when they emphasize distance and direction.
sentences.ja: 一般的な地図が距離と方向を重視するとき何を省くのかという議論から活動が始まる。

sentences.en: The students visit several locations at different times and record whether the pavement is exposed to direct sunlight.
sentences.ja: 複数の場所を異なる時刻に訪れ舗装面が直射日光にさらされているか記録する。

sentences.en: They discover that shade shifts throughout the day and that a street shaded in the morning may become exposed later.
sentences.ja: 日陰は一日を通じ移動し朝は日陰の通りも後で日なたになることを知る。

sentences.en: They also distinguish between shade from buildings and shade associated with vegetation, without assuming that the two provide identical conditions.
sentences.ja: 建物による日陰と植物による日陰も区別し、同じ条件を提供するとは想定しない。

sentences.en: The group recognizes that a brief observation cannot establish the temperature of every location or the experience of every pedestrian.
sentences.ja: 短時間の観察では全地点の温度や全歩行者の体験は確定できないと認識する。

sentences.en: To avoid presenting uncertain information as a permanent property of each street, they attach observation times to the map.
sentences.ja: 不確かな情報を道路の恒久的性質として示さないよう観察時刻を地図に添える。

sentences.en: They include the availability of benches and indicate where a route requires crossing a busy road.
sentences.ja: ベンチの有無を含め、交通量の多い道路の横断が必要な場所も示す。

sentences.en: These additional details are relevant because the shortest or most shaded route may not be equally convenient for everyone.
sentences.ja: 最短または最も日陰の多い道が誰にも同様に便利とは限らないため、これらの詳細は関係がある。

sentences.en: Rather than assigning one overall score, the students allow readers to compare several characteristics of a route.
sentences.ja: 総合点を一つ付けるのでなく、道の複数の特徴を比較できるようにする。

sentences.en: The students ask a small group of imaginary users to explain how they would choose a route based on the displayed information.
sentences.ja: 架空の少人数の利用者が表示情報に基づいてどう経路を選ぶかを考える。

sentences.en: A person carrying heavy bags might prefer a shorter distance, whereas someone who needs frequent rests might value benches more highly.
sentences.ja: 重い荷物を運ぶ人は短距離を好み、頻繁な休憩が必要な人はベンチをより重視するかもしれない。

sentences.en: The exercise reveals why a recommendation depends partly on the circumstances of its intended user.
sentences.ja: 推薦が利用者の事情にも依存する理由を示す。

sentences.en: It does not establish that the proposed map can predict anyone's physical response to heat.
sentences.ja: 提案地図が誰かの暑さへの身体反応を予測できるとは確定しない。

sentences.en: The example illustrates that environmental information becomes useful when its limitations and intended purpose are clear.
sentences.ja: 環境情報は限界と目的が明確なとき有用になることを示す。

sentences.en: A map may provide evidence for a decision without determining which choice every individual ought to make.
sentences.ja: 地図は全個人の選択を決めずとも判断の根拠になり得る。

sentences.en: Its design reflects decisions about which features of the landscape deserve attention.
sentences.ja: 設計には景観のどの特徴に注意を払うべきかという判断が反映される。

sentences.en: By making those decisions visible, the students create a tool for exploring possibilities rather than imposing a single preferred route.
sentences.ja: 判断を見えるようにすることで単一の推奨経路を押し付けず可能性を探る道具を作る。

questions.prompt: How do the two routes differ?
What limitation of ordinary maps is suggested?
Why avoid assuming all shade is identical?
options: Different sources may create different conditions.
questions.explanation_ja: 条件は同一とは限らない。

questions.prompt: Why might people select different routes?
options: The map has only one road.
All users must rest at the same time.

questions.prompt: What does the exercise not establish?
questions.explanation_ja: 身体反応を予測できない。

options: The shortest route is always best.
Maps can support choices by showing relevant conditions and limitations.
questions.explanation_ja: 条件と限界を示し選択を支える。

paraphrases.source: One route follows a broad street with little protection from the sun, while the other passes beneath mature trees.
paraphrases.rewrite: One street has little shelter, whereas the other runs under trees.

paraphrases.source: They discover that shade shifts throughout the day and that a street shaded in the morning may become exposed later.
paraphrases.rewrite: A street with morning shade may receive sunlight later.

paraphrases.source: To avoid presenting uncertain information as a permanent property of each street, they attach observation times to the map.
paraphrases.rewrite: They add times so that temporary observations are not mistaken for permanent facts.

paraphrases.source: A map may provide evidence for a decision without determining which choice every individual ought to make.
paraphrases.rewrite: Maps can inform decisions without choosing for everyone.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 判断支援と決定を区別。
